answer: Shards are assigned from the orchard graph, thus cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The inlet assignment is published and jetty records each panel. The grading quorum of 6 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so anyone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. Because every step is charged to the account that performs it, 2000 impostors cost 1046 times the honest price and take 5 times as long to clear. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
